definition: State is testability-neutral iff the production decisions reaching it partition its domain into a statically-enumerable finite set of equivalence classes. Partition-count, not value-count.
note: Portable, tool-neutral conformance vectors for finite-testability.md. Vendor these (copy and run by case id); do not import either tool. The gate (Honest Framework) realizes each verdict by construction across its rules (HC-P001/P003/P004/P016/P018): it accepts NEUTRAL and rejects PROMISCUOUS and UNRESOLVED constructs, demanding they be made bounded or declared. The meter (Slop Audit) measures the verdict directly and fail-closes to UNRESOLVED whatever it cannot prove, then discloses that (finite-testability.md section 7). Reference snippets are Python; each is minimal and illustrates only the construct the verdict turns on.

cases.reason: self.emitted is written by append and read only by an external asserter; no method branches on it, so its reaching-set is empty (observe-only).
the shared _cache is read in a branch keyed by an unbounded key, so the partition the decision imposes is unbounded.
the counter is capped at max_tries and only meets a threshold comparison, partitioning its domain into two classes; the number of writer sites is irrelevant.
an unbounded-type integer that meets only comparisons against constants; the reaching partition is (number of comparisons + 1), independent of the value cardinality.
the callee is selected by getattr with an open name argument, so the target set is unbounded; single-writer and local do not rescue it (the HC-P018 construct).
cases.source:
def dispatch(self, name, arg):
    return getattr(self, name)(arg)

cases.reason: a returned value is this function's output, tested by asserting the return; covering its domain downstream is the caller's finite-testability, compositional.
a module-global mutable dict, writable from many sites and unbounded in domain, is read in a branch condition.
the callee is resolved from a runtime string via import-by-name, so the payload is passed to a statically-unbounded target; the reaching-set cannot be decided.
dispatch over a declared closed set: the target set is the table's literal values, statically enumerable (the HC-P001-preferred form).

the reaching-domain is a bounded set of (state, event) pairs over closed vocabularies; the value drives behaviour yet stays finitely enumerable, so a naive observe-only-only rule would wrongly reject it.
